items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 62:1
items.html: All the lights of the head shine from the aspect of the Galgalta, for the lights of the Sealed Brain do not ascend there in name, being an aspect lower than it, as is known. And the Galgalta is divided into two heads — the Galgalta and the Avir — because the screen of Atik does not rule over the Galgalta, since it was corrected in the aspect of the MEM, in concealed Hassadim, from which the Yud does not go out of its air ever. And the Avir is the LAMED of Tzelem, and hence concealment and revelation operate in it: in Katnut, the hairs cover it, that is, before the Yud goes out of its air; and in Gadlut, after the Yud goes out of its air and light remains, the forehead is revealed, for the hairs depart from there, as above, Page 368, Items 155-158, see there. And look well at Answer 22 above.
